# The 7 best document scanning software for enterprises in 2026

09/22/2026 15:50
\| [Bärbel Heuser-Roth](https://www.doxis.com/en/blog/authorprofile/heuser-roth)

![Banner featuring the text 'Best Document Scanning Software' with logos of various software providers.](https://www.doxis.com/files/content/images/blog/2026/Best%20Document%20Scanning%20Software.png)

Paper still slows down more of the business than most IT leaders expect. Invoices sit in a scanner queue. Contracts get filed by hand. A records manager spends an afternoon hunting for a signed form that's somewhere in a shared drive, or worse, a filing cabinet down the hall.

According to [AIIM](https://www.doxis.com/en/analyst-reports/market-momentum-index-intelligent-document-processing-idp-survey-2025) (2024), over 45% of business processes remain paper-based, even after years of digital transformation spending. That gap costs more than storage space. It costs the hours a records team spends re-keying data instead of managing risk.

Document scanning software closes that gap, and the AI-powered platforms on the market now do far more than produce a searchable PDF. This guide breaks down the 7 best document scanning software for enterprises in 2026, comparing each on features, integration depth, pros, cons, and pricing.

## **Key takeaways**

1. **Doxis** is the strongest all-around platform, pairing AI-powered document capture with a full content automation suite that scales across SAP, Salesforce, and Microsoft 365
2. **ABBYY FineReader PDF** is the best-known name for standalone OCR accuracy on individual documents and PDFs
3. **M-Files** is the strongest pick for metadata-driven retrieval instead of folder structures
4. **Laserfiche** is the strongest fit for records-heavy compliance and government workflows
5. **DocuWare** is the most accessible mid-market platform for accounts payable and paperless-office projects
6. **Ephesoft** is the most configurable engine for high-volume, mixed-format batch capture
7. **Docsumo** is the sharpest specialist for structured data extraction from invoices and financial documents

## **What is document scanning software?**

Document scanning software converts paper documents into digital files, then uses OCR and AI to make that content searchable, classified, and ready for business workflows. Modern enterprise platforms go beyond image capture: they extract structured data, validate it against business rules, and route documents directly into ERP, CRM, or [document management systems](https://www.doxis.com/en/solutions/document-management).

## **The 7 best document scanning software for enterprises**

The vendors below were selected based on scanning and OCR accuracy, AI-powered data extraction, enterprise integration depth, and independent analyst or reviewer recognition.

### **1\. Doxis**

Doxis brings document scanning and capture together with enterprise content management, workflow automation, and compliance controls in a single platform. Its [AI-powered OCR and data extraction](https://www.doxis.com/en/idp/ocr-data-extraction) reads structured, semi-structured, and unstructured documents, from invoices to handwritten forms, then hands the result straight to [document classification](https://www.doxis.com/en/idp/document-classification), workflow, and [records management](https://www.doxis.com/en/blog/records-management) inside the same system.

Doxis connects natively to SAP, Salesforce, and Microsoft 365, so scanned documents land in the systems teams already use instead of a separate silo.

**Pros**:

- Native, certified integrations with SAP, Salesforce, and Microsoft 365 keep scanned documents inside existing business systems
- AI-powered OCR and data extraction handles structured, semi-structured, and unstructured documents in one step
- Named a Leader in the [Gartner Magic Quadrant for Document Management 2026](https://www.doxis.com/en/analyst-reports/gartner)
- Built-in [records management](https://www.doxis.com/en/blog/records-management) and audit-proof [archiving](https://www.doxis.com/en/business-platform/archiving) apply retention rules automatically, so scanned records stay compliant without manual filing
- Reviewers on Gartner Peer Insights point to the platform's flexibility, citing how components can be distributed across servers and customized down to individual record types ( [Gartner Peer Insights](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/document-management/vendor/doxis))
- Reviewers on G2 highlight the ease of onboarding and having OCR and workflow handled end to end in one platform ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/doxis-ai-dp/reviews))

**Cons**:

- Built for enterprise-scale document volumes and multi-system environments, so a team evaluating only a single-purpose scanning app may find the wider platform more than they need right now

**Pricing**: Custom, based on modules, user count, and document volume. A demo can scope a quote against your own document types.

### **2\. ABBYY FineReader PDF**

ABBYY FineReader PDF is one of the most recognized names in OCR, built for converting scanned paper and PDFs into editable, searchable files. It's positioned as desktop and server-based OCR rather than a full enterprise content platform, so most organizations pair it with a separate document management or workflow system once volume grows past a single department.

**Pros**:

- Consistently rated among the more accurate OCR engines on the market for typed text and complex layouts
- Supports a wide range of languages and preserves original formatting during conversion
- Available as a desktop application or server-based engine for higher-volume deployments

**Cons**:

- G2 reviewers tag the software as expensive relative to its scope, and note it has no free version ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/abbyy-finereader-15/reviews))
- G2 reviewers separately note that OCR accuracy drops on lower-clarity scans, and that the Mac version feels more complicated and less consistent than the Windows version ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/finereader-pdf-for-windows-and-mac/reviews))

**Pricing**: From ~€69/year for the Mac edition. Enterprise server licensing is quoted based on volume and deployment.

### **3\. M-Files**

M-Files organizes documents by metadata rather than folders, which changes how scanned documents get found later. Once a document is scanned and OCR'd, M-Files can classify it automatically and attach the metadata that determines who can access it and how long it's retained. It integrates with Microsoft 365, Salesforce, and several ERPs, making it a common fit for organizations already standardized on Microsoft tools.

**Pros**:

- Metadata-based retrieval removes the need to know which folder a document lives in
- Automated classification and access permissions cut manual tagging work after scanning
- Strong integrations with Microsoft 365, Outlook, and Teams for organizations already in that ecosystem

**Cons**:

- G2 reviewers note that heavy datasets and large vaults can slow performance, and that some everyday actions take extra clicks compared to competitors ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/m-files/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons))
- TrustRadius reviewers separately note that switching between multiple document vaults during search causes confusion, and that retired or superseded documents can still surface in results ( [TrustRadius](https://www.trustradius.com/products/m-files/reviews))

**Pricing**: From $65/user/month for the Essentials tier, per M-Files' published pricing.

### **4\. Laserfiche**

Laserfiche pairs document scanning and capture with strong workflow and records management tools, which makes it a common choice for government agencies, healthcare, and other compliance-heavy sectors. Scanned documents move through configurable workflows for approval, retention, and disposition, with OCR built into the capture step.

**Pros**:

- Deep workflow and business process automation layered directly on top of scanning and capture
- Strong reputation for records management and retention in regulated and government environments
- Reviewers consistently cite fast rollout once workflows are configured

**Cons:**

- G2 reviewers from smaller organizations flag licensing costs as a barrier, particularly under the 25-user minimum on some tiers ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/laserfiche/pricing))
- G2 reviewers separately note a steep learning curve for advanced features like Quickfield, and that document administration can be confusing for new users ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/laserfiche/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons))

**Pricing**: From ~$53/user/month for the Cloud Starter tier, with a 25-user minimum on some plans.

### **5\. DocuWare**

DocuWare targets mid-market organizations running paperless-office and accounts payable automation projects. Its scanning and indexing tools connect with common scanning hardware and mobile capture, feeding an OCR-based intelligent indexing engine that reduces manual metadata entry.

**Pros**:

- Mobile scanning app and hardware-agnostic capture cover both office and remote scanning needs
- Intelligent indexing applies OCR-based metadata automatically instead of manual tagging
- Workflow automation for accounts payable and approvals is included in the core platform

**Cons**:

- G2 reviewers on the Cloud license cite pricing as high relative to included storage, especially as document volume grows ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/docuware/reviews?page=3&qs=pros-and-cons))
- G2 reviewers separately note that initial setup and configuration is complex even for teams already familiar with document management systems, and that mastering indexing and workflow configuration takes time for non-technical staff ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/ricoh-india-ltd-docuware/reviews))

**Pricing**: Custom quote only; DocuWare does not publish fixed tiers.

### **6\. Ephesoft**

Ephesoft Transact is a dedicated capture engine built for high-volume, mixed-format batches: paper, fax, and electronic documents processed side by side. It classifies, separates, and extracts data before handing documents to whatever downstream system a business already runs, which makes it a common fit for service providers processing documents on behalf of multiple clients.

**Pros**:

- Handles structured and unstructured documents in the same batch without separate configuration per format
- Flexible licensing that scales down to mid-sized deployments, not just large enterprise contracts
- Reviewers highlight strong customer support and quick proof-of-concept setup

**Cons**:

- Capterra reviewers note that Ephesoft's documentation has historically lagged behind its more advanced configuration options ( [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/149079/Smart-Capture/reviews/))
- Gartner Peer Insights reviewers separately describe the initial setup as painful, with support sometimes hard to reach during that phase ( [Gartner Peer Insights](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/intelligent-document-processing-solutions/vendor/ephesoft))

**Pricing**: Custom, on request. Ephesoft does not publish fixed pricing tiers.

### **7\. Docsumo**

Docsumo focuses on the data extraction side of scanning rather than the scanning step itself. Feed it invoices, bank statements, or ACORD insurance forms, and it returns structured, validated fields ready for export. It's built for accounts payable and finance teams that need accurate line-item data more than a full document management platform.

**Pros**:

- Pre-trained models for common document types like invoices and bank statements cut setup time
- SOC 2, GDPR, and HIPAA certifications ease procurement sign-off for regulated teams
- Integrates directly with accounting software including QuickBooks Online and Xero

**Cons**:

- G2 reviewers note that advanced configuration and custom model training demand more technical expertise than the base product suggests ( [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/docsumo-docsumo/reviews))
- Capterra reviewers separately note that extraction accuracy can slip when invoice layouts vary widely across a large or diverse document set ( [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/183875/Docsumo/reviews/))

**Pricing**: Usage-based, by document volume. Exact tiers are quoted on request.

## Key benefits of digitizing documents with AI-powered scanning

Scanning alone just creates an image. The real benefits show up once AI-powered extraction and classification are layered on top of it.

- **Faster processing**: Data lands in workflows in seconds instead of waiting for someone to key it in by hand
- **Fewer errors:** AI-based validation catches mismatched totals and missing fields before they reach a downstream system
- **Searchable records:** [OCR text recognition](https://www.doxis.com/en/blog/ocr-text-recognition) turns scanned images into content you can search by keyword, not just browse by folder
- **Lower storage costs**: Digitized [archives](https://www.doxis.com/en/business-platform/archiving) replace physical filing cabinets and off-site boxes
- **Audit readiness**: Automated retention and indexing make it easier to produce the right document the moment an auditor asks for it

## **What to look for in enterprise document scanning software**

Not every platform above solves the same problem, so match the evaluation criteria to what your team actually needs.

- **OCR accuracy on your real documents:** A vendor's headline accuracy number rarely reflects your worst scans, so test it against your own handwriting, stamps, and multi-language forms
- **AI-powered classification and extraction**: Look for [document classification](https://www.doxis.com/en/idp/document-classification) that recognizes document types automatically, not just OCR that produces a searchable image
- **Enterprise integration depth:** Confirm certified connections to SAP, Salesforce, or Microsoft 365 if scanned documents need to reach those systems
- **Compliance and retention controls**: Enterprises in regulated industries need automated retention, legal holds, and audit trails built in, not bolted on afterward
- **Deployment flexibility:** Cloud, on-premises, and hybrid options matter differently depending on data residency and IT policy

## **FAQs on document scanning**

### What is document scanning software?

Document scanning software converts paper documents into digital files, then uses OCR to make the text searchable and editable. Enterprise platforms add AI-powered classification and data extraction on top, so scanned documents can move directly into business workflows.

### How long does it take to implement enterprise scanning software?

Implementation ranges from a few weeks for a single scanning and OCR use case to several months for multi-department rollouts involving custom document types and ERP integration.

### What's the difference between document scanning and document digitization?

Scanning creates a digital image or PDF of a paper document. Digitization goes further, using OCR and AI to extract, classify, and index the content so it can be used in business processes, not just viewed.

### Can document scanning software read handwritten documents?

Some platforms can, using handwriting OCR trained on cursive and printed handwriting, though accuracy still varies with legibility. Test any vendor's claim against your own handwritten forms before committing.

### What's the difference between OCR and intelligent document processing (IDP)?

OCR converts an image of text into machine-readable characters. IDP goes further, using AI to classify the document, extract structured fields, validate the data, and route it into a workflow automatically.

### Is document scanning software GDPR compliant?

Compliance depends on the platform's retention, access control, and data residency options, not the scanning step itself. Look for automated retention rules and GDPR-focused compliance controls rather than assuming compliance is automatic.

### How much does enterprise document scanning software cost?

Pricing varies widely: standalone OCR tools can run under $100 a year, while enterprise platforms with AI extraction, workflow, and compliance built in are quoted based on modules, users, and document volume.

### Can document scanning software integrate with SAP or Salesforce?

Enterprise-grade platforms offer certified integrations with SAP, Salesforce, and Microsoft 365, so scanned documents land directly in the systems teams already use instead of a separate silo.
